target.title: fix(qa): simplify smoke lanes and isolate fanout
target.body:
Related: #101186
Related: #101187
Follows: #102256

## What Problem This Solves

#101186 restored automatic QA Smoke coverage, but its implementation coupled a hardcoded three-row Actions matrix to a second dynamic shard planner, added speculative scenario weights, pinned a scenario count that immediately drifted, and left `subagent-fanout-synthesis` in a shared concurrent suite worker.

That exact scenario failed twice on recent `main` runs while Matrix and the other Telegram shard passed:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28935299128
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28947909491

A first two-lane version of this PR proved that one 93-scenario Crabline job exceeded eight minutes. Setup took only about 40 seconds; the runtime was the per-shard package build plus the full scenario set. This revision bounds the critical path by splitting Crabline into three equal 31-scenario shards.

The targeted scenario contracts from #101187 remain correct: Slack and WhatsApp restart/resume stay live-driver-only, and the silence-sensitive channel baseline stays isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the weighted planner with four explicit bounded lanes: Matrix plus three shards for the current Crabline default channel.
- Partition Crabline deterministically by sorted scenario ID, producing equal 31/31/31 shards today.
- Keep the lane IDs independent of the current Crabline default channel so that channel can change later.
- Fail closed if the smoke profile gains an unsupported third channel instead of silently adding runner fanout.
- Remove the hardcoded scenario total; profile growth is selected automatically.
- Isolate `subagent-fanout-synthesis`, which owns asynchronous child completion delivery and failed inside a shared seven-scenario worker.
- Re-enable both QA Smoke jobs after #102256's temporary action-level kill switch.

## User Impact

Automatic QA Smoke returns with four bounded Blacksmith shard jobs: 5 Matrix scenarios and three Crabline shards of 31 scenarios each. The aggregate required check remains fail-closed and artifact behavior is unchanged.

The additional runner fanout is deliberate: every shard currently pays a roughly 3.5-minute package-build floor, while a single 93-scenario Crabline lane exceeded eight minutes. Three Crabline shards should restore the critical path to roughly the prior 6-8 minute range while keeping the planner substantially simpler than #101186.

## Evidence

- Two-lane exact-head observation: Matrix passed in 4m30s; the 93-scenario Crabline job was still running beyond eight minutes before the superseding push.
- Recent #101186 runtime shape: Matrix completed in roughly 4-5 minutes; each 46/47-scenario Telegram shard completed in roughly 8-10 minutes, including duplicated package builds.
- Focused Testbox after the 31/31/31 split: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28962361871 — planner and workflow guards passed, 38 tests total.
- Earlier focused Testbox: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28960709690 — planner, catalog, suite-planning, and workflow guards passed, 104 tests total.
- Exact failing-batch replay on Testbox lease `tbx_01kx1apqv7ee0ybrjm9mxhn5k1`: 7/7 passed; logs show `subagent-fanout-synthesis` ran in a dedicated `scenarios=1 concurrency=1` worker.
- Fresh clean Testbox changed gate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28961085005 — typecheck, lint, dependency guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview after the four-shard revision: clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.78.
